newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's oil distributor Turcas keeps sales target.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's oil distributor Turcas keeps sales target.

text.p: Turkish petroleum products distributor Turcas Petrolculuk A.S. is adhering to plans to sell 1.3 million tonnes of white petroleum products this year despite competition from cheap Iraqi diesel entering Turkey in cross-border trade, a senior official said.

"We will not revise our sales targets of 1.3 million tonnes of white products and $750 million turnover despite unfair competition from the cheap and tax-free diesel entering from Iraq," Raphael Vermeir, general manager of Turcas, told Reuters.

"If you change targets every month, they are not targets any more and right now we are not distant from these targets. Perhaps this serious level of diesel imports will again become minor border trade," he said.
Turcas shares traded at 8,100 lira on the Istanbul Stock Exchange on Tuesday morning, unchanged from Monday's close. The market index firmed 0.6 percent in the first session.
Unofficial estimates put Iraqi diesel sales in Turkey at around 1.5 million tonnes this year, up sharply from at least 500,000 tonnes in 1996.

The Turkish government allows border trade with Iraq through its southeast gate to help the region's poor peasants, where more than 27,000 trucks bring tax-free Iraqi diesel into the country in exchange for food.

"At end-April, official figures show that diesel consumption in Turkey has gone down by 12 percent. But we all know that it has actually gone up. So we say that the market share of the Iraqi diesel can go as high as 15 to 20 percent," he added.
"Obviously, it is no longer a simple border trade."

Consumption of registered and taxed diesel shrank to 7.2 million tonnes in Turkey in 1996 from 7.7 million tonnes in 1995, when the number of trucks and the amount of Iraqi diesel carried by each truck was one third of current capacities.
Turcas operates 648 Turkpetrol stations, the third biggest network in Turkey after state owned Petrol Ofisi and British Petroleum.
"We invest in both new stations and modernisation of old ones at a total cost of eight to nine million dollars this year," Vermeir said.
"Our aim is to increase our market share by a couple of percentage points, but it is very tough," he added.

He said Turcas's market share in white petroleum products, which include all products except fuel, stood at 8.5-8.6 percent and they targeted 9.0 to 9.5 percent at the highest, because of strong foreign players like Shell and BP.

Vermeir complained about the pricing system in petroleum products in Turkey, where prices are practically imposed by state-owned oil refiner Tupras and distributor Petrol Ofisi(POAS) which are the market makers.
He said private and foreign distributors had several discussions with Turkish authorities to introduce an automatic pricing mechanism but the government had not yet made a move.
"Automatic pricing mechanism is so important in a high-inflation environment, because it helps to keep our margin," Vermeir said.

"But it is also very important for privatisation because there is no way to privatise POAS and Tupras without giving the international community a means to show that prices are controlled by market forces, not by political orders," he added.
The method to be applied when privatising Turkey's petroleum industry is also very important, according to Vermeir.
"Until a method is decided, it will be very difficult for us to judge how the market will be afterwards," he said.

Turcas reported 18.3 trillion lira turnover in the first quarter against 9.3 trillion in the same 1995 period. But its net profits were little changed at 485 billion lira versus 406 billion, despite annual inflation running at around 80 percent.
Vermeir said first quarter profits fell in real terms because Turcas and its lubricant producing arm Turkish Castrol were split after the first quarter of 1996.
The major shareholder Turcas is Canoco Inc's Tabas Petrolculuk A.S. which acquired a 82.16 percent stake last year.
-- Osman Senkul, Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875.
